items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: And so I tried to follow Ellington’s “edit yourself,” and the old “less is more,”

ctx.x: Say, “No, I don’t want double time here.” It’s too late.

Exactly. That’s right. So that’s exactly why I started playing and then later I began playing a secondary keyboard when I could afford another piano player. I was my own mediocrity for a few years, playing very badly. But I was able to maybe not play so much but my hands are big and I can play maybe one beautiful, big change in a chord —in a bar — instead of two or three chords in the bar. And so I tried to follow Ellington’s “edit yourself,” and the old “less is more,” and just encapsulate what I wanted to say…
Well I think the thing you said about being able to speak the language is really important.
